- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., > 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect potential rebound.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., 70+), leading to exaggerated upward momentum in forecast; cap or smooth out such peaks.
- Mean reversion bias: if price has been rising sharply, model often fails to anticipate pullback; add slight downward correction in later periods.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag in capturing sentiment-driven momentum; align forecast with sentiment peaks 1–2 days ahead.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows, model tends to misalign with trend direction; prioritize sentiment-weighted smoothing over raw price trends.
